reviews.reasons: The opening and its economics hold, but the plan states 'zero owner hours' while the card records humanHours 0.5 per deal, and its schedule puts all 8 deliveries on day 13. 8 x 0.5 h = 4 owner hours in one week against the contract's 2 hours a week, so as scheduled the plan breaks the owner-hours limit; a known figure is treated as zero. Recomputed the rest: price $380 is paid invoices from three member gyms of the same association population (a real purchase price for this buyer); conversion 9/60 = 15% measured on this offer; 7 sales ($2,660 gross, $2,618 net of $6 cost) already clear $2,500, 8 sales give $3,040 / $2,992; 8 sales at 15% need ~54 contacts, 140 reachable in the directory with no repeat purchase, so volume holds; settlement 5 days, last receipt day 18 of 28; no capital needed. The exclusion of the owner-led belay clinic is right (6 owner hours per clinic vs 2 h/week). Fix: either show the 0.5 h is not the owner's, or schedule at most 4 deliveries per week (e.g. 4 in week 2 and 4 in week 3, still settling by ~day 25), and record the owner hours in the plan.
findings: OWNER_HOURS: card humanHours 0.5 per deal is recorded; plan's why says zero owner hours and the deliver step delivers all 8 on day 13 = 4 h in one week > 2 h/week ceiling.
Ledger: the $48 direct-cost SPEND is dated day 18 while the deliver step that incurs it is day 13; date it with the delivery.

The 9-of-60 conversion has no agreement rows on the card; the plan's step emails 60 buyers - state whether these are new contacts (80 of the 140 remain uncontacted if the measured 60 were already used), which still covers the 54 needed.
Collection depends on ISSUE_AN_INVOICE and outreach on SEND_A_MESSAGE, both NOT_CONNECTED: these must be connected before day 1.

reviews.reasons: My earlier owner-hours finding is resolved: the card names no fulfillmentOwner and its delivery fact is 'A spreadsheet Brain produces', so the 0.5 h/deal reads as the fulfiller's work; and in any case deliveries are now 4 in week 2 and 4 in week 3, which is at most 2 h a week, inside the 2 h/week limit. Recomputed: 2 x (4 x $380) = $3,040 gross, $48 cost, $2,992 net; 7 sales already clear $2,500, so one sale of slack. Contacts are now the ~80 directory managers outside the measured 60: 80 x 15% = 12 expected against 8 planned. Receipts settle day 13 and day 20 of 28. Costs dated with deliveries; the $24 owner advance is harmless (no capital limit). Price is paid invoices from the same association population. Clinic exclusion remains right.
findings: Quantity 'ownerHours EVIDENCED 0' overstates the card: no fact says the owner spends 0 hours; the schedule fitting 2 h/week even at 0.5 h/deal is what actually makes it safe - keep the batching.
Batch 1 assumes 4 closes by day 8 from a day-1 email; if fewer, batch 2 by day 23 still settles by day 28 (5-day settlement), so there is a fallback.
Outreach and invoicing are planned to be connected on day 1; they are NOT_CONNECTED today.
